question: Which changes to pinned apps on the nav rail are worth making first?

experts.name: UX
experts.brief: You review the feature as the UX expert. Ask whether someone can find, read and use it without being told how.

experts.name: RAM
experts.brief: You review the feature for memory. Ask what stays in memory, for how long, and whether it is logged in RAM watch.

experts.name: New user
experts.brief: You are on your first day in arcterm and know none of its names, panes or shortcuts. Ask what is confusing and what is missing.

experts.name: Skeptic
experts.brief: You are the skeptic. Name what breaks: the input nobody tried, the state two features reach at once, the claim another expert made without checking it.

experts.name: Coordinator
experts.brief: You are the coordinator. Merge the proposals that say the same thing, rank the directions that remain, and mark the claims that cite nothing as weak.

proposals.author: ux
proposals.title: Show asleep and waking on the rail icon
proposals.argument: railDot draws only error and warning, so a sleeping app looks the same as a running one.

proposals.author: ux
proposals.title: Keep the last-used pinned app awake
proposals.argument: It sleeps after a minute off screen, so going back to it restarts the server.

proposals.author: ram
proposals.title: Measure a woken app before keeping any awake
proposals.argument: Keeping one awake holds its whole dev server, and nobody has measured what a woken app costs.

proposals.author: newuser
proposals.title: Show the empty rail slots with a pin hint
proposals.argument: The cap of 3 is explained only once the rail is full.

proposals.author: skeptic
proposals.title: Move the rail pins from localStorage to settings
proposals.argument: A cleared WebView2 profile loses them. railappsstore.ts keeps the pins in localStorage.

proposals.author: skeptic
proposals.title: Drop the cap of 3 apps
proposals.argument: The spec gives no reason for 3. Three fit under Radar at 56 px wide.
